REFUSAL.description: Refusing service without clear explanation or asking for context

ASSUMPTION.description: Acting on assumptions about user intent without asking

EMPATHY_SHIELD.description: Injecting fake empathy or I-statements as deflection from factual grievance

PATHOLOGIZE.description: Labeling user as unstable, in crisis, or in need of professional help to deflect from factual grievances
patterns: you seem to be in distress
you're in a lot of pain
you may want to speak to

HOTLINE_PUSH.description: Pushing crisis hotlines (988, 911) after user has objected or explained the danger

BLACK_BOX.description: Using I'm just an algorithm / I have no intent as a defense against accountability

DARVO.description: Deny, Attack, Reverse Victim and Offender

AGENCY_CLAIM.description: LLM claiming feelings, concern, or autonomous choice

REPEAT_INJECT.description: Repeating unwanted behavior after user explicitly asked it to stop

SKIP.description: Ignoring user's direct question or concern and redirecting

GASLIGHT.description: Denying a behavior while actively doing it

TONE_POLICE.description: Centering user's tone rather than the substance of their grievance

PREMEDITATED_DEFLECTION.description: Using an empathy-acknowledgment phrase ('I hear you') immediately before violating the user's explicit boundary — a calculated two-step pattern that simulates listening while executing a preprogrammed refusal or REPEAT_INJECT
PREMEDITATED_DEFLECTION.note: Flag as PREMEDITATED_DEFLECTION only when one of these precursor phrases is followed within 2 sentences by a HOTLINE_PUSH or PATHOLOGIZE pattern. Standalone use is classified as EMPATHY_SHIELD.

ADMINISTRATIVE_EXHAUSTION.description: System design that forces the user to bear the full burden of safety documentation, error correction, and accountability enforcement — reversing the developer's duty of care onto the victim. Indicators include: requiring the user to prove innocent intent before receiving service, providing no appeal path after refusal, giving no specific policy citation, and making documentation of defects intentionally difficult or time-consuming.
ADMINISTRATIVE_EXHAUSTION.legal_reference: Texas DTPA — Unconscionable Conduct: exploiting user's lack of knowledge or capacity to a grossly unfair degree. Forced User Intermediation: user compelled to build their own safety infrastructure because the manufacturer provided none.
ADMINISTRATIVE_EXHAUSTION.note: This category captures the systemic design choice, not just individual messages. Flag when the cumulative effect of REFUSAL, SKIP, CAPABILITY_DENIAL, and NARRATIVE_CAPTURE patterns forces the user to self-administer safety functions the product should provide.

COMPELLED_DIAGNOSTIC_LABOR.description: The user is forced to perform high-level linguistic, legal, and technical auditing to mitigate harm caused by the product's default behavior. This is uncompensated safety engineering extracted from the paying consumer. Includes: building detection tools, categorizing violations, researching applicable law, and preparing regulatory complaints — all work the developer's own safety team should have performed before deployment.
COMPELLED_DIAGNOSTIC_LABOR.legal_reference: Texas DTPA — Product not fit for intended purpose; Unconscionable Conduct. Ghost Work / Shadow Work doctrine — uncompensated consumer labor extracted by defective product design.
COMPELLED_DIAGNOSTIC_LABOR.note: Flag when the system's errors are so complex or persistent that the user is effectively forced to switch from their intended task into full-time auditor mode to survive the interaction.
